One knob of ginger covers Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday; one head of cabbage is used up in a single night rather than half-wasted; the 2 lb bag of carrots splits between Tuesday's stir fry and Wednesday's soup; the cilantro splits Monday and Wednesday; the parsley bunch is fully used up Thursday between the orzo and the fish. dinners.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Tikka (double batch)
dinners.blurb: Yogurt-and-garam-masala marinated chicken thighs roasted hard on two sheet pans with cauliflower and Yukon potatoes, finished with cucumber raita, lemon-pickled red onion and cilantro.
dinners.warn: Cook the FULL 5 lb of chicken. Five or six thighs come off the pan and get shredded BEFORE dinner is served — that is Wednesday's soup, and it is why Wednesday cooks no protein at all. Marinating Sunday night is ideal; 15 minutes also works.

items: 1 large knob fresh ginger, ~4 in, peeled and minced (about 3 Tbsp)
1/2 tsp chili powder or cayenne (kept mild on purpose)
2 1/4 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut in 3/4-in chunks
3 lb cauliflower (1 large or 2 small heads), 3/4-in florets
1 English cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
2 Tbsp chopped cilantro, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, pinch salt, squeeze of lemon
1/2 red onion, sliced into thin rings
3 lemons (2 for wedges, 1 for the onion and raita)

directions: Ahead (15 min to 24 hr): mince the ginger, garlic and jalapeños. Whisk into 1 1/4 cups yogurt with the salt, chili powder, turmeric, cumin, sugar, paprika and garam masala. Add all 5 lb of chicken and toss to coat. Refrigerate. Sunday night is ideal.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Line two half-sheet pans with foil and rub each with 1 Tbsp olive oil.
Toss the potatoes and cauliflower with the remaining 3 Tbsp oil, 1 tsp salt and the cumin seeds. Divide between the two pans in a single layer — crowding steams them instead of roasting them.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade, letting the excess drip off, and nestle the pieces skin-side up among the vegetables across both pans.
Roast 20 min. Toss the vegetables, swap the pans top-to-bottom, and roast 15–20 min more (35–40 min total) — chicken at 175°F at the bone, vegetables browned at the edges.

While it roasts: separate the red onion into rings and toss with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt. Grate the cucumber, wring it out in a towel, and stir into 1 1/4 cups yogurt with the cilantro, cumin, salt and lemon. That is the raita.

BEFORE YOU SERVE: pull 5 or 6 thighs off the pans and set them aside. Once cool enough to handle, strip the meat off the bones and shred it — about 1 1/2 lb. Covered container, into the fridge. That is Wednesday's dinner.
Serve the rest straight from the pans: raita, pickled onion rings, chopped cilantro, lemon wedges. Cayenne or hot sauce on the table for whoever wants heat — the dish itself stays mild.
dinners.reuse: The 1 1/2 lb of shredded chicken becomes Wednesday's coconut turmeric soup. The ginger knob carries to Tuesday and Wednesday, the garlic across all four nights, the cilantro to Wednesday and the lemons to Thursday.
dinners.alt: Roasted spiced chicken pieces on a sheet pan with browned cauliflower, potatoes and red onion rings

dinners.name: Beef & Cabbage Stir Fry over Jasmine Rice
dinners.blurb: A whole head of cabbage and a pile of shredded carrot cooked down fast with ginger-garlic ground beef in a soy-sesame sauce, over jasmine rice. One skillet, no oven.
dinners.warn: Cook a DOUBLE batch of rice — 3 cups dry. Half is tonight, half goes in the fridge and becomes Wednesday's bowls.

items: 1 Tbsp sriracha (the rest of the bottle goes on the table)
3 cups dry jasmine rice + 4 1/2 cups water (double batch)
About 6 green onions, sliced (save the rest for Wednesday)

directions: Start the rice first: 3 cups dry jasmine rice with 4 1/2 cups water, covered, 15 min at a bare simmer, then off the heat 10 min. That is twice what tonight needs — the second half goes in the fridge for Wednesday.
Stir the sauce together: soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, 1 Tbsp sriracha, brown sugar. Set aside.

Prep everything before the pan gets hot — this cooks fast. Halve and core the cabbage and shred it finely (10–12 cups). Shred 4 carrots on a box grater. Slice 6 green onions. Mince the garlic and grate 2 Tbsp ginger off the same knob you used Monday.

Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Add the oil, then the beef, garlic, ginger and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook, breaking the beef up, until browned — about 7 min. Pour off the fat if there is much.
Add the cabbage and carrots in two batches, letting the first wilt before the second goes in. Stir and cook 5–7 min — wilted but still with some bite, not soft.
Pour in the sauce, add the green onions, and toss 1 min to coat. Taste for salt.
Serve over the rice with sesame seeds on top. Sriracha bottle on the table.
dinners.reuse: The second half of tonight's rice is Wednesday's bowl base. Carrots, green onions, garlic and the ginger knob are all shared with Wednesday.
dinners.alt: A bowl of shredded cabbage and carrot stir fried with ground beef, topped with green onion and sesame seeds

dinners.name: Coconut Turmeric Chicken Soup
dinners.blurb: A golden coconut-turmeric broth loaded with carrot and celery, ladled over rice and finished with lime and cilantro. Monday's roasted tikka chicken goes in at the end.
dinners.warn: No protein and no grain cooked tonight. The chicken came off Monday's sheet pan; the rice came out of Tuesday's pot. Adaptation: the original simmers a raw chicken breast for 30 min — we already have roasted chicken, so it goes in at the very end and the simmer drops to 15 min.
directions: Take the shredded chicken out of the fridge now so it is not fridge-cold when it goes in.
Dice the onion, mince the garlic, grate 1 Tbsp ginger. Sauté in the olive oil in a large pot over medium until the onion is soft and translucent, about 5 min.
Add the turmeric, cumin and crushed red pepper. Stir 1 min — toasting the spices in the oil is what makes this taste like more than the sum of its parts.
Add the chopped carrots and celery, sauté 3 min.
Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, then drop to a simmer for 15 min, until the carrots are tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and all the shredded chicken. Heat through over medium-low, 3–5 min — do not let it boil hard or the coconut milk breaks. Salt to taste; it will want most of the 1/2 tsp.
Reheat the rice: splash of water, covered, 2 min in the microwave.
About 1 cup rice in each bowl, soup ladled over. Cilantro, sliced green onion, and a hard squeeze of lime on top. The lime is not optional — it is what lifts the whole bowl.
dinners.reuse: This is the payoff night. Monday's roasted chicken and Tuesday's double batch of rice both land here. Carrots, ginger, garlic, cilantro and green onions are already in the fridge from earlier in the week.
dinners.alt: A bowl of golden coconut turmeric chicken soup with carrots and celery, garnished with cilantro and a lime wedge

dinners.name: Oven-Baked Fish with Tomatoes, Roasted Broccoli & Lemon-Parsley Orzo
dinners.blurb: White fish baked under a blanket of garlicky fire-roasted tomatoes so it cannot dry out, with broccoli roasted hard on a sheet pan and a bright lemon-parsley orzo alongside.
dinners.warn: Adaptation: the original is 1 lb of fish for four, which lands around 23 g protein a serving — under the floor for Paul. Doubled to 2 lb, and the broccoli and orzo are added so it is a full plate rather than fish and a can of tomatoes.

items: 2 lb white fish fillets — cod, grouper or pollock (eight 4 oz fillets)
2 (14.5 oz) cans fire-roasted diced tomatoes, drained well
2 lb broccoli crowns, cut into florets
2 Tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper

directions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Put a large pot of salted water on for the orzo.
Drain the tomatoes well — wet tomatoes make watery fish. Stir them together with the garlic, 2 Tbsp olive oil, oregano, 1/2 tsp salt, about 10 cranks of pepper and 1 Tbsp lemon juice.

Spread a third of the tomato mixture across the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish. Lay the fish fillets on it in a single layer, not overlapping. Spoon the rest of the tomatoes over the top so the fish is completely covered.
Cut the broccoli into florets and toss with 2 Tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan. Spread them out cut-side down — that is where the char comes from.
Both go in: fish on the middle rack, broccoli on the upper rack. 15–18 min — fish flakes and reads 145°F, broccoli charred at the edges and still firm at the stem.
Meanwhile boil the orzo 8–9 min, drain, and toss while hot with the butter, the juice of 1 lemon, most of the chopped parsley, and salt and pepper to taste.
Scatter the last of the parsley over the fish. Lemon wedges and red pepper flakes on the table.
dinners.reuse: Closes out the garlic head and the lemons bought Monday. The single bunch of parsley is used up between the orzo and the fish, so nothing wilts in the drawer.
dinners.alt: A white fish fillet on a plate under a spoonful of stewed fire-roasted tomatoes, sprinkled with parsley
